column1: Maintains the 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent target range and signals patience amid a strong labor market and solid activity, with inflation running below 2 percent. Beige Book reports across Districts point to only modest growth in March–April, with mixed consumer spending among general retailers and auto dealers, manufacturing weighed by trade-related uncertainty, and agricultural conditions strained by heavy rainfall and flooding. Complementing this, the April 2019 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows banks tightening standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and broadly tighter terms, alongside weaker demand for construction/land development, HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans (with auto and subprime mortgage demand roughly unchanged). Consistent with the May 2019 Financial Stability Report, equity volatility had eased by May but vulnerabilities linger. These Beige Book and credit insights temper the otherwise positive labor and activity signals, making the overall tone cautiously positive rather than neutral-positive. sentiment score = 0.18
